newsitem.title: ECUADOR: U.S. envoy warns that corruption grips Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy warns that corruption grips Ecuador.

text.p: U.S. ambassador to Ecuador Leslie Alexander said on Wednesday that "deep-seated corruption" was taking over the South American nation and could harm the flow of U.S. investments there.

"One U.S. businessman made a complaint to the embassy that to get out of customs some merchandise worth $8,000 he had to pay a bribe of $12,000," the envoy said in a speech to a local chamber of commerce.
"The worst thing is that corruption is growing and becoming systemic," he said. "And that upsets me because Ecuador is getting a reputation for deep-seated corruption."
The U.S. envoy urged the government of President Abdala Bucaram, who was voted into power last year, to fight corruption or put foreign investments in the Andean country at risk.
